newsitem.title: GERMANY: Gold seen in $340-425 trading range 1997 - West LB.
newsitem.headline: Gold seen in $340-425 trading range 1997 - West LB.

text.p: Gold bullion prices in 1997 were seen in a very broad trading range of $340 to $425 dollars per ounce amid high volatility, WestLB bank said in a report.
"Big price moves in both directions are likely," it said.
The bank said gold was under options-related downside pressure and further overshadowed by mine sales and the possibility of European central bank selling.
But on the other hand, it was oversold and underpinned by Japanese buying in response to the yen's weakness against the dollar.
Also, the central banks' room for manouevre was limited as their gold inventories were priced closely to the market and there was little scope to win additional profits.
WestLB said Germany's Bundesbank had rejected the idea of sales from the country's gold reserves and France and Italy were also unlikely to sell their gold reserves into the market.
Belgium, which did sell gold in recent years, had said the auctions had been completed.
Only the Spanish and Portugese positions were as yet unclear.
Silver prices had been dragged down by gold and were now undervalued because they were not reflecting a potential physical supply deficit, WestLB also said.
Existing stocks in Europe and the U.S. were not readily available at current prices.
Plays on the gold-silver ratio could also give it an upside bias.
Silver's 1997 price range was put at $4.50-6.50 an ounce.
The platinum price range in 1997 could be $350-450, WestLB said.
The metal should keep its premium over gold, or even extend it, as many more countries were making platinum-bearing autocatalysts mandatory.
